steps.action: Open the sign-in page and authenticate with the assigned validator account
steps.expected: An authenticated session is established for the email-delivery surface
steps.observed: Login succeeded and the browser navigated from /dashboard back to the authenticated queue fixture URL.

steps.action: Open /email-delivery?tab=queue&queueFixture=loading and inspect the queue tab on initial load
steps.expected: A visible loading skeleton or loading copy appears before the queue settles
steps.observed: DOM inspection found visible loading copy including 'Loading email queue' and 'Refreshing queued jobs…' with one active skeleton placeholder before the settled queue content rendered.

steps.action: Switch away to Delivery Log, return to Queue, and trigger the manual refresh control
steps.expected: The queue loading state can be surfaced again deterministically during follow-up fetches
steps.observed: Returning to Queue and clicking Refresh current tab both reproduced the visible 'Refreshing queued jobs…' state while the queue fixture was loading.

evidence.network: Browser resource inspection during refresh showed authenticated fetches to /api/ops/email-delivery and /api/ops/email-delivery?summaryOnly=1 while the queue tab displayed the loading indicator; agent-browser network capture did not separately record the queue request.
evidence.domEvidence: Visible loading copy matched 'Loading email queue' and 'Refreshing queued jobs…'; DOM inspection also reported skeletonCount=1 during both initial load and queue re-entry.

frictions.description: agent-browser network request capture returned 'No requests captured' for the queue surface, so network evidence had to be gathered from in-page resource timing and DOM inspection instead.
frictions.resolution: Used agent-browser eval to inspect loading text, skeleton presence, current URL, and recent resource entries after reproducing the loading state.

summary: Retested VAL-Q-006 in a fresh authenticated browser session. The queue fixture reliably surfaced visible loading text and a skeleton on initial load, after tab re-entry, and during manual refresh, so the assertion passed with fresh screenshot and DOM evidence.
